office_does: The State Senator is the 26th District's single member of the Washington Senate, voting on state law and budgets and confirming gubernatorial appointments.
race_blurb: Democratic Senator Deborah Krishnadasan, who won a 2025 special election, faces Republican Gary Parker, a Gig Harbor restaurant owner and former Intel executive making his first run. Both campaign against tax increases; they differ on spending, public safety, climate and reproductive policy.

candidates.summary: Senator since 2025 and former Peninsula School Board president, running on lowering costs, school funding and reproductive rights.
highlights: Voted against ESSB 6346 (2026 tax on millionaires) and the major 2025 revenue bills [S5][S10][S11]
Prime sponsor of SB 6162, expanding property tax relief for seniors and disabled veterans [S14]
Supports strong legal protections for abortion; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S1][S3]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parental-rights list [S6][S7]

taxes.basis: Voted nay on ESSB 6346 and on the 2025 gas, B&O, capital gains/estate and services tax bills; campaigns on voting no on tax increases and proposing a sales tax cut.

spending.basis: Cites new energy assistance, PreK Promise funding, and added support for healthcare and childcare programs.

housing.basis: Supports expanding affordable housing and protecting renters and first-time homebuyers.

safety.basis: Pairs funding for law enforcement officers with behavioral health and community-based violence prevention.

climate.basis: Supports 'bold but balanced climate action' and clean energy jobs.

experience.basis: Sitting senator since 2025 and former school board president, against a first-time candidate.

immigration.basis: Campaign lists banning ICE from wearing face masks among her actions.

healthcare.basis: Supports capping drug prices and fair reimbursement within the current system and offsetting federal Medicaid cuts.

social.basis: Supports strong legal protections for abortion and cites emergency-room reproductive care legislation; endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yea on ESHB 1296's amendments to the I-2081 parental-rights list; her stated view that families should have a voice does not address notification or opt-outs.

candidates.summary: Gig Harbor restaurant owner, former Intel engineer and executive, and Rotary president, running as 'Not a politician' on affordability and public safety.
highlights: Lists tax relief and property tax among his priorities and wants seniors 'not taxed out of their homes' [S1][S2]
Criticizes 'out-of-control spending' and pledges responsible use of taxpayer dollars [S3]
Calls for fully funding law enforcement [S2][S3]
Would expand energy supply and remove regulatory barriers to housing [S3]

taxes.basis: Campaigns on tax relief and fighting rising taxes, asking how much of what people earn 'belongs to the government'.

spending.basis: Criticizes 'out-of-control spending' and pledges transparency and responsible spending.

housing.basis: Would increase housing availability by removing regulatory barriers.

safety.basis: Calls for fully funding law enforcement and says state policies have made it easier for criminals to exploit the system.

climate.basis: Would expand energy supply to stabilize energy prices.

experience.basis: No elected experience; campaigns as 'Not a politician' against a sitting senator.

reform.basis: Says serving means saying no to outside special interests; touts a campaign without paid consultants.
